step.text: NHS Lothian: 4 steps after you complain; free help is offered
step.detail:
NHS Lothian says complaints should be raised with them first so they can try to resolve the issue quickly and as close to where it happened as possible. If it is not resolved, they use a two-stage complaints procedure and, if you are still unhappy after the investigation, you can refer it to the Ombudsman.
1. Stage 1 – Early Resolution: straightforward complaints are aimed to be resolved within five working days, unless there are exceptional circumstances.
2. Stage 2 – Investigation: more serious or complex complaints, or ones not resolved at Stage 1, move to investigation.
3. NHS Lothian acknowledges the complaint in writing within three working days and may telephone you to discuss your concerns and what outcome you want.
4. If you remain unhappy after the investigation, you can refer the complaint to the Ombudsman (SPSO).
No free complaint support service is mentioned on these pages.

Drafted. Location: Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Accident & Emergency department. Outcome: An explanation of what went wrong, treatment or support to put things right and compensation for what happened.

I am complaining about the care I received at the Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh, Accident & Emergency department.

In early July 2026, I fell on my outstretched hand and attended A&E at the Royal Infirmary. My wrist was X-rayed, I was told it was a sprain, and I was sent home.

The pain did not go away. In mid August 2026, my GP sent me back, and a second X-ray showed a scaphoid fracture.

In October 2026, I missed my second-year exams and had to stop shifts at my part-time job because I could not use my wrist.

In November 2026, the fracture had still not healed and I now need surgery.

I would like an explanation of what happened between my first attendance in early July 2026 and the later finding of a scaphoid fracture in mid August 2026.

I would also like to ask about the NICE NG38 Fractures (non-complex) recommendation: "Consider MRI for first-line imaging in people with suspected scaphoid fractures following a thorough clinical examination." Please can NHS Lothian explain how this was followed in my care, and whether a scaphoid fracture was suspected at my first A&E attendance.
